significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish a form-(iii) law—factual-retrieval accuracy decreases with "subject token count" even within language and resource level—plus a form-(ii) mechanism in which the impairment is "causally localized to early-layer subject-token aggregation." This would fix predictions for which entity queries should fail and explain why, combining a behavioral phenomenon with a causal mechanism; that coupling matters because X-FACTR documents cross-lingual retrieval gaps while ROME-style causal tracing treats subject-token enrichment as part of factual recall. The claim is determinate, and a negative result would also be useful by ruling out fragmentation itself as an independent explanation and redirecting attribution toward exposure, resource level, or decoding rather than merely reporting a failed search. In the topic-substitution check, the generic multilingual-representation topic would not license this specific controlled scaling relation or causal locus, so the score is supported by claim-specific content rather than the topic's importance.

reach.justification: The transferable handles are the measurable "subject token count (fertility)" as a vulnerability predictor and the proposed "subject-representation pooling / retokenization" intervention; fertility is ex ante because it can flag risky entity queries before retrieval, while pooling or retokenization provides an inference-time action. Unlike a model-specific direction alone, the asserted relation—more fragmentation predicts poorer knowledge access after controlling for language and resources—would still predict the qualitative finding after tokenizer-specific re-extraction on another multilingual model. The hypothesis is framed across multilingual models and languages, with plausible uptake by model auditors, tokenizer designers, and deployment practitioners who need to screen entity-name reliability, although it does not specify a universal quantitative coefficient or threshold. After substituting away the claim and leaving only the topic, neither this predictor nor the mitigation rule remains, so the reach score does not derive from multilinguality itself.
